Merges are always applied to whatever `HEAD` currently points to in the checkout you run the command in — you `cd` into (or use) the worktree tracking the release branch and run `git merge feature-branch` there. You never run the merge from the feature-branch worktree, since that would merge the release branch into the feature branch instead, and you don't need a separate worktree just to "have access to" the feature branch — see below.

**Relationship between worktrees' object databases:** they aren't separate — all worktrees created with `git worktree add` share a single object database. Only one repo's `.git/objects`, `.git/refs`, and `.git/config` exist; each worktree gets its own private `HEAD`, index, and working directory (tracked under `.git/worktrees/<name>/`), but commits, blobs, trees, and branch refs are visible from every worktree instantly, with no fetch/pull/push needed between them. That's why the merge doesn't require "syncing" the feature branch into the release worktree first — the feature branch's tip commit is already present in the shared object store the moment it exists in any worktree. The only hard constraint is that git won't let the same branch be checked out in two worktrees at once (to avoid two working trees diverging on one ref).
